question_text: Ms. Hammond put the names of all her students in a hat. The probability that she will pull out a boy's name at random is 3 out of 7. There are 12 girls in the class. How many boys are in Ms. Hammond's class?

So, there are 21 total students in the class. If 12 of them are girls, there are 21−12=9 boys.

question_text: The floor of Room A is in the shape of a square and has an area of 144 feet². The floor of Room B is in the shape of a rectangle and has a length of 9 feet and width of 15 feet. Which statement correctly compares the floors in the two rooms?
diagram_description: none
choices: The area of the floor in Room A is the same as the area of the floor in Room B.
The area of the floor in Room A is the less than the area of the floor in Room B.
The perimeter of the floor in Room A is less than the perimeter of the floor in Room B.
The perimeter of the floor in Room A is equal to the perimeter of the floor in Room B.

official_solution: The correct answer to the question is answer choice (D), The perimeter of the floor in Room A is equal to the perimeter of the floor in Room B. Since the area of the square floor in Room A is 144 feet², and we know that all side lengths equal, the side length = 12 feet. Thus, the perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 feet. The area of the floor in Room B (9 × 15) is less than 144 feet², so answer choices A and B can be eliminated. question_text: Jeff is practicing his long jumps for the track team. His first jump measured 3 yards, 1 foot, 2 inches. His second jump measured 2 yards, 3 feet, 3 inches. His final jump measured 3 yards, 15 inches. Which statement about these jumps is true? (1 yard = 3 feet; 1 foot = 12 inches)
diagram_description: None.
choices: Jeff jumped further in his first jump than in his second.
Jeff jumped further in his second jump than in his first.
Jeff jumped the same distance in his first and final jumps.
Jeff jumped the same distance in his second and final jumps.
correctness_strip: Same strip; maroon = 11,20,24,29,31,37.
topic_specific: mixed-unit length conversion and comparison (yards/feet/inches)
notes: Answered correctly.
official_solution: The correct answer to the question is answer choice (A), Jeff jumped further in his first jump than in his second. Begin by trying to simplify the measurements. Jeff's first jump cannot be simplified. He jumped 3 yards, 1 foot, 2 inches. In his second jump, since 3 feet = 1 yard, we can say Jeff jumped 3 yards, 3 inches. In his final jump, since 12 inches = 1 foot, we can say Jeff jumped 3 yards, 1 foot, 3 inches. Now, order the jumps. 3 yards, 3 inches < 3 yards, 1 foot, 3 inches < 3 yards, 1 foot, 2 inches. So, second jump < first jump < final jump.
